newsitem.title: UK: Scottish Widows says neutral on devolution.
newsitem.headline: Scottish Widows says neutral on devolution.

text.p: Scottish life insurer Scottish Widows said on Friday it was neutral on the subject of devolution for Scotland.
"On the issue of devolution, we neither back it or oppose it," group chief executive Mike Ross said in a statement.

"We would not presume to express a view on the merits or otherwise of any particular constitutional arrangement provided our concerns in respect of fiscal and regulatory cohesion are addressed," he added.
The question of whether Scotland should have some level of political devolution is one of the more controversial issues of the present election campaign in Britain.
Scottish Widows said it issued the statement after a number of interpretations had been made of its views on possible constitutional change in Scotland.
The Scotsman newspaper said today that the statement followed comments by Trade Secretary Ian Lang that Scottish Widows was not comfortable with devolution.
Edinburgh based Standard Life, one of the largest UK life insurers, told Reuters that it was also adhering to its long-held neutral stance on devolution.
Newspaper reports earlier this week that Standard Life supported devolution were incorrect, a spokeswoman said.
